title: ObjectDisposedException on exit when evaluate_js called after WebView2 disposed
description:
On exit, pywebview throws ObjectDisposedException when evaluate_js is invoked after the WebView2 window has already been disposed:

  File edgechromium.py line 146, in evaluate_js
    self.webview.Invoke(...)
  System.ObjectDisposedException: Cannot access a disposed object.
  Object name: 'WebView2'

This happens because the orchestrator continues pushing UI updates (e.g. agent status, beads item closure) after the window teardown has begun. Fix: guard evaluate_js calls with a disposed/alive check, or stop pushing UI updates once the window is closing.
close_reason: Fixed by architecture - desktop_ui.py no longer uses evaluate_js. Uses direct in-process method calls via pywebview.api polling pattern. Shutdown sets _is_running=False preventing further calls.

title: Add desktop app build verification to pre-commit hooks
description: Add a pre-commit check that verifies the desktop app builds successfully (vite build) when desktop files are staged. Currently check-build.ps1 only validates Python syntax. The check should: (1) Detect staged desktop/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,css,html} files. (2) Skip if none are staged. (3) Run 'npm run build' in the desktop/ directory (which runs tsc -b && vite build). (4) Fail the commit if the build fails. This catches import errors, missing modules, and Vite config issues that tsc alone might miss. Can potentially be combined with the type-check into a single build step since 'npm run build' already includes tsc -b.
notes: Added desktop build verification to check-build pre-commit hook

Output should be a single-folder distribution that can run without a system Python installation. Must include pywebview and its WebView2 dependency.

title: Pre-flight health checks and self-repair before work submission
description: In run 20260224_171341, 11 items were submitted to a broken environment after maintenance left stale locks and dirty repo state. All failed silently with 0 agent requests. A circuit breaker would only delay retries against the same broken state. Instead, implement health-gated work submission: (1) Before each work batch, run pre-flight checks: verify git status is clean, worktrees are creatable, required locks are available, disk space is sufficient. (2) If pre-flight fails, attempt automatic self-repair: clear stale locks (verify holder PID is dead), reset dirty git state, prune orphan worktrees. (3) If self-repair fails, log a detailed diagnostic and shut down gracefully rather than submitting doomed work. (4) Classify errors as environmental (stop all work) vs item-specific (skip item, continue). This replaces PokePoke-sjm6 which was framed as a circuit breaker.

title: Agent SDK sessions silently die without recording failure
description:
In run 20260309_141908_18b81e96, 5 of 8 agents silently stopped producing output mid-work with no error, no completion status, and no orchestrator log entry recording their death. The orchestrator kept running (showed 'active=8' in poll logs) but the agents were already dead.

Evidence from the run:
- worker-7 (j8r5): Last log at 14:27:57, was mid-edit on config.py. No error recorded.
- worker-1 (0gy0): Last log at 14:33:19. No error recorded.
- worker-3 (un8k): Last log at 14:36:25. No error recorded.
- worker-4 (ig7o): Last log at 14:37:00. No error recorded.
- worker-8 (aumh): Last log at 14:58:40, was mid-test-run. No error recorded.
- Only 3 agents (workers 2, 5, 6) completed successfully.
- Orchestrator log shows only 2 'Completed work item' entries and stops at 14:55:46.
- No timeout, drain, orphan, or circuit breaker messages in orchestrator log.
- A zombie python process (PID 17500) remained running but produced no output.

The orchestrator poll loop showed 'active=8 max=8 slots=0' until 14:47, meaning it believed all 8 agents were running when at least 4 had already silently died ~20 minutes earlier.

Impact:
1. UI shows agent cards stuck at last activity with no indication the agent died
2. Work items remain assigned to dead agents (in_progress status never cleared)
3. Orchestrator wastes slots on dead agents instead of reclaiming them for new work
4. No error telemetry - impossible to diagnose root cause without manual log analysis
5. User sees agents 'working' in the UI for an hour when they actually died silently

Needed:
- SDK session health monitoring (heartbeat/ping) to detect dead sessions
- Timeout on SDK sessions that produce no tool calls for N minutes
- Record explicit failure when an agent session ends without completion
- Clear agent status in UI when session death is detected
- Unassign work items from dead agents so they can be reclaimed
close_reason: Added SDK session inactivity detection. _await_completion now monitors last_event_time and aborts sessions that produce no SDK events for session_inactivity_timeout seconds (default 600s). Dead sessions return explicit failure, freeing orchestrator slots and triggering work item unassignment.

title: Confusing UI for gate agent retry cycle
description:
The terminal UI for gate-agent-driven retries is hard to follow. Looking at PokePoke-bajj (rainbow_boa-worker-2) as an example:

1. Version numbering is backwards/unclear - the cards show v1, v2, v3 but the chronological order in the UI makes it hard to tell which attempt is which. The gate agent cards (v1 Gate Agent, v2 Gate Agent) interleave with work agent cards (v2, v3) in a confusing way.

2. The GATE FAILED badge appears on what looks like a completed card with 'Added comment', 'Restarting Work Agent with feedback', making it unclear whether the item ultimately succeeded or failed.

3. When the gate agent rejects work and the work agent retries, there is no clear visual separation between attempts. The user sees a stream of cards (work v1 -> gate v2 rejection -> work v2 retry -> gate v1 passed) with no obvious timeline or grouping.

4. The gate agent rejection reason is truncated and requires expanding to understand what happened, but even expanded it is mixed in with other workers' output.

5. Suggestion: Group retry attempts visually (e.g. 'Attempt 1', 'Attempt 2'), show a clear retry arrow/indicator between attempts, and make the final outcome (pass/fail) prominent at the top of the card group rather than buried in the middle of the timeline.

title: Duplicate merge logic in worktree_finalization.py and worktree_merge_handler.py causes behavioral divergence
description:
## Summary

worktree_finalization.py (merge_worktree_to_dev, lines 92-187) and worktree_merge_handler.py (_handle_worktree_merge_inner, lines 53-174) contain nearly identical merge-attempt-cleanup-retry logic that has already diverged in behavior.

## Divergences Found

1. **Conflict details**: worktree_finalization.py builds a detailed conflict_details string with file list for the cleanup agent prompt; worktree_merge_handler.py does not, giving the cleanup agent less context
2. **Conflicted file display**: finalization shows up to 10 files, merge_handler shows up to 5
3. **Manifest tracking**: merge_handler tracks failed worktrees via add_uncleaned_worktree(); finalization does NOT, leaving orphaned worktrees untracked
4. **Repo root**: finalization uses Path.cwd() (fragile, depends on caller cwd); merge_handler takes repo_root as parameter (correct)
5. **Import style**: finalization uses late imports inside function body; merge_handler uses imports at function top
6. **Return type**: finalization returns bool; merge_handler returns tuple[bool, bool] (merge_success, worktree_cleaned)

## Impact

- **Orphaned worktrees**: Items processed through worktree_finalization.py that fail to merge are NOT tracked in the manifest, so cleanup never finds them. Disk usage grows silently.
- **Maintenance burden**: Any bug fix or behavior change must be manually mirrored in both files. The divergences above show this is already failing.
- **Inconsistent cleanup agent prompts**: One path gives the cleanup agent detailed conflict info, the other doesn't, leading to different success rates depending on which code path runs.

## Fix

Extract the shared merge-attempt-cleanup-retry pattern into a single function (e.g., in a new merge_logic.py or consolidate into worktree_merge_handler.py). Both call sites should delegate to the shared implementation. The merge_handler version is closer to correct (uses parameters, tracks manifest, returns cleanup status).
close_reason: Consolidated duplicate merge logic into perform_worktree_merge

title: Desktop UI: Add tag management section for special-effect tags (human-required, high-conflict-risk)
description: Add a section in the Desktop UI that displays a list of available special-effect tags and allows users to add/remove them from work items. Special-effect tags modify how the orchestrator handles items - for example: 'human-required' causes the orchestrator to skip the item (needs human), 'high-conflict-risk' (from PokePoke-a8nm) would serialize execution to avoid merge conflicts. The UI should: (1) Show available special-effect tags with descriptions of their effects, (2) Allow adding/removing tags on work items, (3) Visually distinguish special-effect tags from regular labels, (4) Show which items currently have special-effect tags applied.

title: execute_merge_sequence does not restore original branch on failure
description: git_operations.py execute_merge_sequence() does git checkout target_branch then git pull --rebase then git merge. If the merge fails, the caller is left on target_branch - there is no try/finally to restore the original branch. Combined with beads stash pop logic, a failure during merge leaves the repo dirty on the wrong branch. Subsequent operations that assume they are on their working branch will operate on target_branch instead, potentially corrupting it. The beads stash may also be silently lost if the process crashes between stash push and pop.
close_reason: Work merged into master - merge sequence improvements completed in prior commits

title: Code Review: beads stash recovery nukes working tree
description:
Problem:
restore_beads_stash (src/pokepoke/git_helpers.py, lines 61-66) runs `git checkout -- .` whenever `git stash pop --index` conflicts. That helper is invoked automatically after each orchestrator pull to restore .beads, so a conflict in .beads forcibly resets the ENTIRE working tree, wiping unrelated tracked edits and untracked files outside .beads.

Impact:
A routine stash conflict instantly destroys the developer's work and leaves the repo inconsistent, which is a high-severity data-loss bug. The helper should only intervene on .beads, not rewrite every file.

Suggested Fix:
Limit the cleanup to the .beads path (e.g., `git checkout -- .beads/` or restore via pathspec) and drop the repo-wide checkout. Alternatively, checkout only the stash paths you need and only drop the stash once recovery succeeds.

title: Add merge locking to worktree finalization and agent runner
description: Wrap merge operations in acquire_lock('merge') to serialize worktree merges. Two call sites: (1) worktree_finalization.py merge_worktree_to_dev() - wrap the merge_worktree() call and conflict resolution in a single lock, (2) agent_runner.py _run_worktree_agent() - wrap the merge section. Default timeout 300s. Agents queue and wait their turn.
close_reason: Superseded by PokePoke-gdsa (merge queue coordinator) which provides a more comprehensive solution with queuing, rebase-between-merges, and failure handling. Simple lock wrapping is subsumed by the full merge queue design.

title: Move bd sync outside claim lock in assign_and_sync_item — wastes agent slot for up to 180s
description: In beads_management.py, assign_and_sync_item() holds a per-item filelock (beads-claim-{id}, timeout=0), and inside that lock calls run_bd_sync_with_retry() which can take up to 3x60s=180s. The sync is best-effort visibility, not correctness-critical — the claim is already verified before sync runs. Move the bd sync call outside the lock scope so the agent slot is freed immediately after claim verification succeeds. Impact: in parallel mode, one hung bd sync blocks an agent semaphore slot for up to 3 minutes, reducing effective parallelism.

title: Shutdown watchdog os._exit(130) bypasses all cleanup, can corrupt merge state
description: In shutdown.py line 194, the watchdog thread calls os._exit(130) after the grace period (5s + 3s per agent). This is a hard process kill that: (1) Skips all finally blocks and context managers - any in-progress merge is left in a half-committed state with merge markers in the working tree, (2) Does not flush file handles - beads_item_stats_store and model_stats_store JSON files can be partially written and corrupted on next load, (3) Leaves file locks held (filelock-based coordination locks become stale), (4) Orphans child processes (git, copilot CLI) on Windows since os._exit does not propagate signals to the process group, (5) The merge queue shutdown thread (line 76-81) is a daemon thread that gets killed when the watchdog fires, so pending merges are silently dropped. With 3 agents running, the watchdog fires after just 14 seconds. Since merges have 60-120 second timeouts, a Ctrl+C during a merge almost guarantees the watchdog fires mid-merge. Fix should replace os._exit() with a cooperative shutdown that waits for the merge lock to be released before force-killing, and ensures stats store writes are atomic (write-to-temp + rename).
close_reason: Implemented: cooperative shutdown watchdog (no os._exit), reliable merge-queue shutdown, and atomic stats-store writes

title: Code Review: repo-filtered model history truncates results
description:
Problem:
get_model_history in src/pokepoke/desktop_api_stats.py (lines 114-171) calls load_model_history_entries(limit=limit) and *then* filters entries by repo_name. When repo_name is provided, the first `limit` rows are usually a mix of repos, so filtering after the fact often returns far fewer results (even zero) despite older entries existing for that repo just past the limit. The UI therefore shows empty history for active repos once other repos fill the latest window.

Impact:
Per-repo trend charts and history inspectors silently truncate data and frequently show nothing for busy repos, making debugging impossible once more than ~limit entries exist globally.

Suggested Fix:
Apply the limit after filtering: continue reading until the filtered list reaches the limit or exhaust the file, or plumb repo_name into load_model_history_entries/model_stats_store so the backend filters before slicing.
notes: Already fixed in commit e25f126. load_model_history_entries filters by repo_name during reading and applies limit afterward. Regression tests exist.

title: desktop_api.py: inconsistent lock usage - 6 public methods mutate shared state without acquiring _lock
description:
## Problem

DesktopApi (desktop_api.py) has an RLock (self._lock) that is used by some methods (push_log, clear_logs, get_logs_since) but NOT used by 6 public state-mutation methods:

- push_work_item() (line 170)
- push_agent_name() (line 191)
- push_progress() (line 195)
- set_session_start_time() (line 178)
- set_session_end_time() (line 183)
- set_live_session_stats() (line 187)

These methods are called from agent worker threads (parallel mode) while get_state() reads all these fields from the UI polling thread without holding the lock. This creates a window where get_state() can observe logically inconsistent state (e.g., work_item from agent A but agent_name from agent B).

## Current Risk

Under CPython's GIL, individual attribute assignments are atomic, so this doesn't cause crashes today. However:
1. get_state() reads are not atomic across multiple fields - UI can show inconsistent combinations
2. Python 3.13+ introduces free-threading (PEP 703, no-GIL mode) which makes these real data races
3. The inconsistent lock pattern is confusing - developers can't tell which fields need protection

## Recommended Fix

1. Wrap all state-mutation methods in 'with self._lock:' blocks
2. Wrap get_state() field reads in 'with self._lock:' to ensure consistent snapshot

title: merge_worktree reports failure after successful git push if post-push verification fails
description:
## Problem

In `worktrees.py` lines 153-163, after a successful `git push`, the merge verification check can fail and return `(False, [])`:

```python
subprocess.run(["git", "push"], check=True, ...)  # Push SUCCEEDS
print(f"Pushed {target_branch} to remote")

# Verification can fail even though push succeeded
if not is_worktree_merged(item_id, target_branch):
    print(f"Merge confirmation failed")
    return False, []  # Returns FAILURE despite successful push!
```

## Impact

- The merge is already pushed to remote, but the orchestrator treats it as a failure.
- The work item is NOT marked complete and will be re-processed.
- Re-processing creates duplicate merges or merge conflicts with the already-pushed work.
- The `is_worktree_merged` check uses `git branch --merged` which can have transient issues (e.g., refs not yet updated after push).

## Fix

After a successful push, treat verification failures as warnings rather than hard failures. Alternatively, use a more reliable check (verify the task branch HEAD is an ancestor of the target branch via `git merge-base --is-ancestor`).

```python
if not is_worktree_merged(item_id, target_branch):
    logger.warning(f"Post-push merge verification failed for {branch_name}, but push succeeded")
    # Don't return failure - the push already happened
```

## Files
- `src/pokepoke/worktrees.py` lines 153-163

title: Code Review: gate_agent_enabled flag ignored
description:
## Problem
`ProjectConfig.gate_agent_enabled` (src/pokepoke/config.py:185) is never referenced anywhere else in the repo. `process_work_item` (src/pokepoke/workflow.py, gate agent block around line 234) always calls `run_gate_agent(...)` after cleanup, so disabling the flag in pokepoke.config.yaml has no effect.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Set `gate_agent_enabled: false` in pokepoke.config.yaml (or via CLI arguments).
2. Start the orchestrator and process any work item until the work agent finishes successfully.
3. Observe that after cleanup the gate agent still launches (status cards + console output) even though the flag is false.

## Impact
Teams that need to temporarily bypass the gate agent (e.g., during emergencies or while debugging flaky gate prompts) cannot do so. Every item still incurs the gate run, which burns additional requests/time and blocks desired workflows.

## Suggested Fix
Wrap the gate agent block in `process_work_item` with a `if not config.gate_agent_enabled` check: log that gate verification is disabled, set `gate_success = True`, skip calling `run_gate_agent`, and break out of the retry loop. That will make the config option functional again.
notes: Fix already implemented: workflow.py line 237-240 checks config.gate_agent_enabled and skips gate agent when disabled. Tests exist in test_config.py and test_workflow.py.

title: Code Review: parse_repos_cli breaks Windows paths
description:
Problem:
parse_repos_cli (src/pokepoke/repo_config_loader.py, lines 101-137) blindly calls entry.split(":") to separate the path from key=value options. On Windows the drive letter introduces a colon, so an argument such as `C:\src\repo:weight=5` is split into path `"C"`, option `"\\src\\repo"`, and `weight=5`. RepoConfig then points to `C`, validation fails, and multi-repo CLI cannot be used on Windows at all.

Impact:
Every Windows user (our primary deployment environment) gets invalid repo paths when supplying absolute paths with --repos, so the feature is broken before validation even runs.

Suggested Fix:
Detect drive-letter prefixes (e.g., use pathlib.PureWindowsPath) or split only on the first colon *after* the path segment. One simple approach is to split once on the first colon not followed by a slash/backslash by using partition or regex, leaving the drive letter intact before parsing weight/max_worker options.

title: Add max_parallel_agents config and thread pool orchestrator loop
description: Replace the sequential while-loop in orchestrator.py run_orchestrator() with a concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor. Add a max_parallel_agents config parameter (default 1 for backwards compat, configurable via CLI --max-agents N and pokepoke.config.json). The orchestrator loop becomes: (1) fetch ready items, (2) filter already-claimed and human-required, (3) submit up to max_parallel_agents - active_count new futures to the pool, (4) collect completed futures, update stats, trigger maintenance. Each future runs process_work_item() for one item. Use a threading.Semaphore(max_parallel_agents) as the throttle. Key constraint: the main orchestrator thread must remain responsive to shutdown signals and UI message processing. Current single-item flow: select_work_item() -> process_work_item() -> maintenance. New flow: select_multiple_items(N) -> submit each to pool -> collect results -> maintenance. Existing code in orchestrator.py lines ~80-130 (the while loop) is the primary change site.

title: Orchestrator polling loop floods logs with redundant check/fetch cycles every 8 seconds
description: During run 20260220_133831_cd6a9414, the orchestrator log shows continuous Checking main repository status + Fetching ready work from beads pairs every ~8 seconds even when all 5 worker slots are full and no new work can be submitted. Between 13:40 and 13:44 alone there are 30+ redundant poll cycles. The orchestrator should either: (a) use exponential backoff when all slots are full instead of constant 8s polling, (b) use event-driven notification when a worker completes instead of polling, or (c) at minimum suppress duplicate log lines (e.g. log once then only log when state changes). This creates enormous log noise that makes debugging harder and wastes I/O.

title: SDK client shutdown can block agent thread indefinitely when copilot process hangs
description:
In copilot_sdk.py (lines 312-319), when the initial client.stop() times out after 10 seconds, the fallback calls client.stop() AGAIN without any timeout. If the copilot subprocess is truly stuck (e.g., waiting on I/O, deadlocked), this second call hangs indefinitely, blocking the agent thread forever.

**Impact:** Each hung agent permanently consumes a slot in the ThreadPoolExecutor. Over time, multiple stuck agents can exhaust all parallel slots, making the system unable to process new work items. This is a progressive degradation that's hard to detect since there are no errors logged.

**Root cause:** Line 315 calls await client.stop() without asyncio.wait_for() timeout wrapper.

**Fix:** Wrap the fallback stop in asyncio.wait_for() with a shorter timeout (e.g., 5s), and if that also fails, forcibly kill the copilot subprocess via its PID. Something like:
  try:
      await asyncio.wait_for(client.stop(), timeout=5.0)
  except TimeoutError:
      logger.warning('Force-killing copilot process after double timeout')
      # Kill subprocess by PID if accessible from client
      
**Affected file:** src/pokepoke/copilot_sdk.py lines 312-319

title: UnicodeDecodeError in subprocess _readerthread using cp1252 codec
description: subprocess.communicate() reader thread crashes with UnicodeDecodeError when reading process output that contains bytes not valid in cp1252 encoding (byte 0x9d at position 70016). This happens because Python on Windows defaults to the system locale codec (cp1252) for subprocess pipes instead of UTF-8. The crash occurs in threading._bootstrap_inner -> subprocess._readerthread -> fh.read() -> codecs.charmap_decode. This likely affects copilot CLI output or git command output that contains Unicode characters (emoji, special chars). Fix: ensure subprocess pipes use encoding='utf-8' and errors='replace' or errors='backslashreplace' to handle arbitrary byte sequences gracefully. Additionally, a follow-on error occurs: 'Failed to backfill beads item stats: the JSON object must be str, bytes or bytearray, not NoneType' - likely because the subprocess output was None/lost due to the reader thread crash.
notes: Fixed: Added encoding='utf-8' and errors='replace' to all subprocess.run() calls. Added None guard in backfill.

title: Code Review: repo picker crashes on headless environments
description:
## Problem
pick_repo_directory() only catches ImportError around the tkinter UI setup (src/pokepoke/repo_picker.py lines 45-127). On headless servers/CI (no DISPLAY) tkinter imports fine but 	k.Tk() raises _tkinter.TclError: no display name and no  environment variable. Because the exception isn't caught, the frozen binary exits with a stack trace before falling back to the console prompt.

## Impact
The new repo picker makes the packaged CLI unusable anywhere without a GUI (SSH session, CI job, Windows Server Core). Users cannot select a repo or run agents even though the previous build worked in these environments.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Build the PyInstaller binary (pyinstaller packaging/pyinstaller/pokepoke.spec).
2. On a headless machine (or run with DISPLAY= on Linux/macOS), execute the binary with no --repo argument.
3. The process crashes immediately with _tkinter.TclError and never shows the fallback prompt.

## Suggested Fix
Catch 	k.TclError (and other runtime exceptions) around the tkinter code path and fall back to the existing console prompt the same way the ImportError branch does. Optionally detect headless environments before instantiating Tk to avoid throwing in the first place.

title: Parallel agents need merge sequencing to prevent merge conflict cascades
description: During run 20260220_133831_cd6a9414, 5 parallel agents all completed work on separate worktree branches and attempted to merge back to master around the same time. This caused: (1) worker-2 hit a delete/modify conflict on .pokepoke/beads_item_stats.json during merge because worker-3 had already untracked it, (2) worker-5 had to resolve worker-2's incomplete/pending merge on master before it could merge its own branch, (3) the orchestrator detected uncommitted changes on master at 13:50 (from merge residue) and launched a heavyweight cleanup agent. We need a merge queue or sequencing mechanism so that when multiple agents finish around the same time, their merges to master are serialized and each merge starts from a clean, up-to-date master. Options: (a) a merge queue that agents enqueue into when done, processed FIFO, (b) a lock-based approach where only one merge runs at a time, (c) rebase-before-merge with automatic conflict detection and retry. This should also coordinate with cleanup agents so they don't run concurrently with merges.
close_reason: Implemented merge lock to serialize concurrent merges from parallel agents

title: Desktop UI: Separate active and completed agent cards into distinct sections

Currently all agent cards are mixed together regardless of state, making it hard to focus on what's actively happening. The completed section should be collapsible and show a summary (e.g., count of completed items, success/failure status).

title: Code Review: parallel single-shot keeps processing entire queue
description:
## Summary
Commit dbd2a24 removed the nd not (not continuous and any_success) guard inside run_parallel_loop() when replenishing slots (src/pokepoke/parallel.py:266-278). In non-continuous mode we now continue to select new items every time a worker finishes, so a single-shot parallel run drains the entire ready queue instead of stopping after the first success. This regresses the documented CLI behavior where default runs handle one bead unless --continuous is supplied.

## Impact
Running python -m pokepoke.orchestrator --autonomous --max-agents N now processes every ready work item in one session. Teams expecting a single bead to be claimed end up with multiple beads assigned, multiple branches created/merged, and much longer unattended runs. Sequential mode still stops after one item, so behavior diverges depending on --max-agents.

## Repro
1. Queue 3+ ready beads.
2. Run python -m pokepoke.orchestrator --autonomous --max-agents 3 (no --continuous).
3. Observe via logs that as soon as the first agent completes successfully, the orchestrator immediately refills its slot and keeps going until the queue empties instead of exiting the session.

## Expected
Non-continuous parallel runs should stop launching new work once any agent succeeds, mirroring the sequential orchestrator. After existing futures drain the session should finalize.

## Suggested Fix
Restore a guard so the replenishment block is skipped once continuous is False and we have already reported a success (e.g., track a session-level has_success flag or reuse ny_success). Alternatively trigger should_stop_after_current() once a success is recorded so the loop drains and exits without claiming new beads.

title: Preflight repair git commit hangs indefinitely - pre-commit hooks block with 60s timeout
description: When launching the orchestrator (python -m pokepoke.orchestrator --autonomous --continuous --max-agents 2), preflight_repair.py attempts 'git commit -m chore: auto-commit for pre-flight health check' which triggers pre-commit hooks. The hooks take longer than the 60s subprocess timeout, causing TimeoutExpired. This retries twice and then crashes the orchestrator. Additionally, the pywebview WebView2 instance throws System.ObjectDisposedException ('Cannot access a disposed object') during shutdown, and fails to clean up its temp user data folder. Two issues: (1) preflight_repair.py L33 runs git commit with a 60s timeout but pre-commit hooks (tests, coverage, linting) can easily exceed that under load. Should either increase timeout, skip hooks for preflight auto-commits, or avoid committing during preflight entirely. (2) Desktop UI WebView2 disposal race: evaluate_js called after webview is already disposed, suggesting the UI thread and orchestrator thread shutdown ordering is wrong.

title: Core orchestration modules have 0% test coverage despite being the critical execution path
description:
orchestrator.py (279 stmts), parallel.py (234 stmts), workflow.py (224 stmts), merge_queue.py (174 stmts), and work_item_selection.py (104 stmts) all show 0% line coverage in coverage.json. These are the heart of PokePoke - the main loop, parallel execution engine, work item processing, and merge coordination.

Tests exist (test_orchestrator.py, test_parallel.py, test_workflow.py) but they are so heavily mocked via @patch that the actual production code never executes during test runs. For example, test_parallel.py patches process_work_item, so workflow.py is never called; test_orchestrator.py patches nearly every dependency.

This is 1,015 uncovered statements across 5 modules that control: agent lifecycle, worktree creation, retry logic, merge coordination, and error recovery. Any regression in these modules goes completely undetected.

Recommended fix:
1. Add integration-style tests that exercise real code paths with minimal mocking (mock only external I/O: subprocess, filesystem, beads CLI)
2. Target 60%+ coverage on orchestrator.py, parallel.py, and workflow.py as first milestone
3. Test critical paths: the main loop iteration, agent failure handling, retry logic, and shutdown coordination

title: Orchestrator stops launching agents after all 10 + janitor finish in continuous mode
description:
OBSERVED in run 20260223_103717_31235e8f (autonomous, continuous, max-agents=10):

TIMELINE:
- 10:37:17 - Orchestrator started, 10 parallel workers launched staggered (10:37-10:47)
- 10:48:28 - First worker completed. Tech debt agent starts.
- 10:49-10:51 - Workers 2-4 complete.
- 10:53:34 - Tech debt completed. Backlog cleanup tries to start but repo dirty (logProcessor.ts UU merge conflict + backfill_beads_item_stats.py untracked). Waits ~3min, times out, skipped.
- 10:56:35 - Code review also blocked by dirty repo (.pokepoke/config.yaml modified). Waits ~3min, times out, skipped.
- 10:59:42 - Auto-commit git add fails due to .git/index.lock (concurrent git process). Cleanup agent launched.
- 11:00-11:02 - Workers 5-6 complete.
- 11:06:05 - Cleanup agent resolves dirty state. Ready work fetched.
- 11:06:07 - Janitor Agent starts in maintenance slot.
- 11:06-11:27 - Workers 7-10 complete (some with 2 agent requests).
- 11:28:19 - Janitor Agent FAILED.
- 11:28:19 - Worktree cleanup tries to start but repo dirty (8 files, UU StatsPage.tsx merge conflict). Waits ~3min, times out, skipped.
- 11:31:21 - Worktree cleanup skipped. Session counter logs 3 then 4 (not 10).
- 11:31:21 - Janitor maintenance tries again but repo still dirty (8 files).
- LOG ENDS AT LINE 465 mid-janitor-dirty-wait. No shutdown message, no continuous loop restart.

ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS:
1. After all 10 workers + maintenance finished, orchestrator should loop back to fetch ready work and launch a new batch. Instead the log just stops - no continuous loop iteration occurred.
2. Persistently dirty repo (UU merge conflicts from concurrent worker merges) blocked ALL maintenance agents (backlog_cleanup, code_review, worktree_cleanup, janitor) - each waited ~3min then skipped.
3. .git/index.lock contention happened during the run from concurrent git operations.
4. Orchestrator process exited with code 1 - likely crashed or exited after maintenance phase without triggering continuous loop.
5. No graceful shutdown log entry - consistent with an unhandled exit path.

CONTRIBUTING FACTORS:
- Merge conflicts (UU status files) left by workers are never cleaned up, permanently blocking maintenance
- The janitor agent itself failed, which may have been the trigger for orchestrator to exit instead of loop
- Session counter shows wrong count (3, 4 instead of 10) suggesting possible state tracking bug

title: Code Review: process_work_item cleanup crashes before metrics import
description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. Trigger any exception in process_work_item before the inline import executes (e.g., make get_config() or select_model_for_item() raise).
2. The function exits through the finally block, which unconditionally calls set_current_work_item_id(None).
3. Because the import never ran, the name is undefined and Python raises UnboundLocalError instead of the original failure, so cleanup/unassign never runs.

Impact:
- The real root cause is masked by UnboundLocalError, so operators cannot see why startup failed.
- The finally block aborts before cleanup_worktree/unassign logic executes, leaving worktrees dirty and beads items stuck as assigned.
- Any early failure in workflow.process_work_item now wedges the system.

Code reference:
- src/pokepoke/workflow.py lines 52-75 import set_current_work_item_id inside the try block, but lines 272-279 in the finally block always call it.

Suggested fix:
- Import set_current_work_item_id at module scope (or before the try) so the name is always bound, or guard the cleanup call.

title: Model stats file corruption under multi-process concurrent writes
description: model_stats_store.py record_completion() uses a threading.Lock (_lock) to serialize read-modify-write of the JSON stats file (lines 137-141). This protects against concurrent threads within a single process, but in multi-agent mode with --max-agents > 1, multiple worker PROCESSES can race on the same file. Two processes can both read, modify, and write the stats file, causing the second write to overwrite the first's changes (lost update). The atomic os.replace() on line 129 prevents corruption but not lost records. Fix: use the existing filelock-based coordination system (coordination.py acquire_lock) to serialize cross-process access, or switch to an append-only JSONL format that avoids read-modify-write entirely.

This makes it clear which maintenance agent spawned the sub-agent and keeps related activity grouped together.

title: Shutdown watchdog can hang forever when merge lock is stuck
description: The watchdog thread in shutdown.py (lines 209-210) waits indefinitely for the merge lock to be released before force-killing the process. If the merge lock holder is hung (e.g., stuck subprocess), the watchdog never fires, leaving the process permanently hung. The while merge_lock_active(): time.sleep(1.0) loop has no maximum timeout. Fix: add a max timeout (e.g. 120s) to the loop so os._exit(130) is eventually reached even when the lock is stuck.

title: Worktree merge/cleanup partial failures leave repository in inconsistent state
description:
Multiple code paths in the worktree merge and cleanup pipeline can fail partway through, leaving the repository, worktree manifest, and beads item status in mutually inconsistent states. This creates orphaned worktrees, dangling branches, and items stuck in assigned state.

Specific failure modes found:

1. **worktree_finalization.py line 71-73**: Catches generic Exception from commit count check (git rev-list) and proceeds with merge anyway. If git is failing (resource exhaustion, timeout), proceeding with a merge on potentially invalid state risks data corruption.

2. **worktree_merge_handler.py line 150+220**: merge_worktree(cleanup=True) called, and on success the function returns (True, True). But cleanup=True doesn't guarantee the worktree directory was removed - worktree_cleanup.cleanup_after_merge can return False on Windows lock errors. The caller reports success while the worktree directory persists on disk.

3. **worktree_merge_handler.py line 196-201**: After cleanup agent runs, if merge is still in progress, abort_merge() is called. If abort fails (line 198-200 returns False), the function returns (False, False) but the repo remains in a merge-in-progress state. Subsequent merge attempts from other workers will fail because the repo is stuck.

4. **worktree_merge_handler.py line 210-211**: On retry failure after cleanup, abort_merge() is called with no error handling. If it fails, the repo stays in merge-in-progress state silently.

5. **workflow.py finally block**: cleanup_worktree() and unassign_with_retry() failures are caught at debug/warning level. If both fail, the worktree is orphaned AND the beads item stays in assigned state permanently (no other agent can claim it).

Impact: Over time, these partial failures accumulate: orphaned worktrees consume disk, stuck-assigned items become permanently blocked, and merge-in-progress state blocks all subsequent merges until manual intervention.

Recommended fix: Add a post-merge state verification step that checks (a) worktree directory actually removed, (b) branch cleaned up, (c) repo not in merge-in-progress state, (d) beads item status consistent. Log errors at ERROR level (not debug) when cleanup fails so issues are visible. Consider a periodic reconciliation job that detects and repairs inconsistent state.
close_reason: Fixed: partial merge/cleanup failures no longer leave inconsistent state

title: Bare exception swallowing hides failures across 15+ critical code paths
description:
**Problem:** The codebase has 15+ instances of `except Exception: pass` or `except Exception:` followed by silent continuation (no logging, no propagation). These are spread across critical operational code paths including cleanup agents, merge conflict handling, process management, and state persistence.

**Impact:** When things go wrong in production, the error trail goes cold at these swallowing points. This creates 'debug blindness' — failures in agent cleanup, state loading, and process management are silently eaten, making root cause analysis nearly impossible.

**Most critical instances (verified):**
- `cleanup_agents.py:136,150,213` — cleanup operation failures silently ignored
- `process_utils.py:23` — process management errors hidden
- `maintenance_state.py:26` — state file loading errors hidden
- `desktop_api_ext.py:41` — config/log root discovery failures hidden
- `frontend_discovery.py:41,112,134` — frontend asset discovery errors hidden
- `repo_utils.py:29,62` — repository utility errors hidden
- `sdk_event_handler.py:50` — SDK event handling errors hidden

**Note:** Several other bare except blocks in the codebase are fine — they either re-raise (agent_runner.py:244, workflow.py:251, maintenance_scheduler.py:231) or are in teardown/cleanup paths where swallowing is defensible (copilot_sdk.py session abort, orchestrator finally block).

**Suggested fix:** Replace bare `except Exception: pass` with `except Exception: logger.debug(...)` at minimum. For critical paths like cleanup_agents and process_utils, use `logger.warning()` to surface the error. This is a low-risk change — it only adds observability without changing control flow.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. All 15+ identified instances have at minimum `logger.debug()` calls
2. Critical path instances (cleanup_agents, process_utils, maintenance_state) use `logger.warning()`
3. No existing tests break
4. Coverage maintained at 80%+
close_reason: Fixed all 19 instances of bare exception swallowing with proper logging

title: MergeQueue future double-set race condition causes crash on shutdown
description:
In merge_queue.py, there is a race condition between _process_request() (line 198) and _drain_on_shutdown() (line 214) that can cause an InvalidStateError crash during shutdown.

Scenario: The worker thread is processing a merge request and calls future.set_result() at line 198. Simultaneously, the shutdown path sends a sentinel (line 120), and _drain_on_shutdown() is called (line 151/157). If the same request's future has already been resolved by _process_request, _drain_on_shutdown will attempt to set_result() again on the same future at line 214, raising InvalidStateError.

This is possible because: (1) _process_request calls future.set_result AFTER the queue.get() removes the item, (2) shutdown can trigger _drain_on_shutdown from TWO places - line 151 (sentinel received) and line 157 (loop exit), (3) there is no synchronization between the future.set_result calls.

Fix: Guard future.set_result() with future.done() check, or use a lock around future resolution:

if not request.future.done():
    request.future.set_result(result)

Key file: src/pokepoke/merge_queue.py, lines 198, 214
Severity: Critical - process crash during shutdown with pending merges
notes: Fixed merge queue future double-set race by guarding future.set_result() in both _process_request and _drain_on_shutdown, added regression tests to ensure already-resolved futures do not raise InvalidStateError during shutdown, and all pre-commit validations passed.

3. Each stage is independently testable with mocked dependencies
4. The top-level function becomes a thin orchestrator calling stages in sequence

title: merge_queue: unhandled exception in _process_request orphans Future and kills worker thread
description:
In merge_queue.py _process_request (lines 173-240), the Future.set_result() call at line 240 is only reached if execution flows through the try/except Exception block (lines 216-238). However, multiple calls BEFORE that block can raise exceptions that escape _process_request entirely:

1. get_default_branch() at line 184 - calls subprocess, can raise on git timeout/failure
2. is_high_conflict_risk(item) at line 177 - reads beads data, can raise
3. is_worktree_clean(worktree_path) at line 191 - calls subprocess, can raise
4. add_uncleaned_worktree() at lines 199-203 - if this raises before set_result at line 204

When any of these raise, the exception propagates through _worker_loop (line 167 has no exception handler), killing the worker thread. Consequences:

- The CURRENT request's Future is never resolved - any caller blocking on future.result() hangs forever
- _drain_on_shutdown() at line 170 never executes - ALL remaining queued requests' Futures are also orphaned
- The worker thread dies silently - is_running returns False but queued items are lost
- New submit() calls restart the worker, but previously queued items are gone

This is a production reliability issue: git timeouts during merge processing (already observed in PokePoke-kpvn logs) would trigger this exact scenario.

Fix: Wrap the entire body of _process_request in try/except BaseException to guarantee the Future is always resolved. Also wrap the _process_request call in _worker_loop with exception handling to keep the worker alive. Example:

def _process_request(self, request):
    try:
        ...existing logic...
    except BaseException as exc:
        if not request.future.done():
            request.future.set_result(MergeResult(status=MergeStatus.FAILED, item_id=request.item.id, message=str(exc)))
        raise

In _worker_loop:
    try:
        self._process_request(request)
    except Exception:
        logger.exception('Unhandled error in merge worker')
        # Worker stays alive for next request
close_reason: Fixed unhandled exception bug in merge_queue._process_request. Added comprehensive exception handling to prevent Future orphaning and worker thread death. All tests pass.

title: Maintenance agents launch while parallel work items are still in-flight
description:
run_periodic_maintenance() is called inside record_fn (orchestrator.py:91), which fires as soon as any single worker completes. This triggers maintenance without waiting for all active parallel workers to finish.

Observed in run 20260219_125559_5d130fb2:
- 13:10:57: worker-4 completed item beads_ui-e2md with SUCCESS (1 request)
- 13:10:57: record_fn fires, items_completed threshold hit, maintenance starts
- 13:10:57: Tech Debt Agent launched (ran until 13:17:05)
- 13:10:57: worker-5 had JUST been submitted and started for the same item
- 13:10:58: worker-5 failed
- Throughout 13:10:57-13:17:05: workers 1 and 3 for beads_ui-b300 were still running (worker-3 log shows writes until 13:21:50)

Maintenance agents (especially Janitor/Worktree Cleanup) interact with git worktrees and beads state that active workers depend on. Running them while workers are in-flight can cause resource contention.

Root cause: In orchestrator.py around line 91, run_periodic_maintenance() is invoked inside record_fn which is called from _collect_done_futures() immediately when any item completes. There is no check of len(futures) == 0 or active_ids being empty before triggering maintenance.

Fix: Either (a) move maintenance check to after _collect_done_futures so it is gated on active worker count being below a threshold, or (b) always wait for all in-flight workers to complete before invoking non-parallel-safe maintenance agents when they are due.
close_reason: Fixed: Maintenance agents no longer launch while parallel workers are in-flight

title: Parallel agent replacement logic launches only one substitute instead of replenishing to limit
description:
## Problem

When initial parallel agents exit (whether by completion or failure), the agent replacement/replenishment logic only launches **1 new agent** instead of replenishing back up to the configured maximum.

If max_parallel_agents=10 and all 10 initial agents exit, only 1 replacement launches instead of up to 10 more.

## Impact

- Severe under-utilization of worker capacity  
- System designed for parallel work degrades to quasi-serial execution
- Wasted potential for throughput improvement
- After initial batch fails, orchestrator essentially idles

## Evidence

From run: C:\Users\ameliapayne\icm_queue_c#\.pokepoke\logs\20260224_150927_b72ade52
- 10 initial workers launched: workers 1-10 (15:29:52-15:31:53)
- Workers 2-10 exit with failures between 15:35:05-15:35:32
- Worker 1 also exits around this time
- Only 1 replacement agent launched: worker-11 at 15:35:40
- Expected: Workers 11-20 should have been launched to replenish to limit
- Actual: Orchestrator enters polling loop with no new agents spawned

## Root Causes to Investigate

1. **Agent pool replacement logic** - May only increment by 1 instead of by (limit - current)
2. **Exit event handling** - May not detect when batch of agents exits together
3. **Startup rate limiting** - May have cooldown that prevents rapid agent spawning
4. **Status tracking** - May lose count of exited agents, not realizing capacity is available

## Solution

1. Track active agent count separately from queued/failed counts
2. When agent exits, check: (max_parallel - currently_active) = agents_to_spawn
3. Launch minimum of [ready work items, agents to spawn] together, not serially
4. Add verbose logging for agent lifecycle: startup, exit, replacement decisions

description:
Problem:
- src/pokepoke/merge_queue.py (lines 151-277) tracks metrics in self._stats but never resets it outside __init__.

title: Code Review: Copilot process cache hides running processes after tasklist failure
description:
## Problem
`check_copilot_processes()` (src/pokepoke/process_utils.py lines 15-48) now caches the result of *every* poll for five seconds. When the `tasklist` subprocess throws (TimeoutExpired, UnicodeDecodeError, etc.), the except block logs a warning, forces `count = 0`, and still sets `_copilot_process_cache = (now, count)`. All subsequent callers within the TTL reuse that cached zero without re-running `tasklist`.

Before this change, a transient tasklist error still returned 0 for that single call, but the next poll re-ran tasklist and observed the real count. After the caching change, a single timeout suppresses the real process count for five seconds, so the orchestrator immediately believes there are no copilot.exe processes even though dozens may still be shutting down.

## Impact
`wait_for_process_cleanup()` now short-circuits as soon as the first `tasklist` call fails under load. The orchestrator then moves on while Copilot is still running, which is exactly what produces `.git/index.lock` contention and locked worktree cleanup. The new caching logic therefore re-introduces the race this commit was trying to eliminate.

## Recommendation
Do not cache failure results. Only populate `_copilot_process_cache` when `tasklist` succeeds, or store an explicit “failure” flag that forces the next caller to re-run the command immediately. At a minimum, reset `_copilot_process_cache` to `None` inside the exception handler so transient failures do not mask still-running processes.

This creates a dangling worktree: a directory that still exists and looks like a git worktree, but whose backing branch has been deleted. Recovery requires manual git worktree prune and directory deletion. The fix is to skip branch deletion when the worktree directory still exists and removal has failed. The branch should only be deleted after confirming the worktree directory is fully removed. This primarily affects Windows where file locking is more aggressive, but the logic error exists on all platforms.

title: Failed item unassign has no retry or recovery, leaving items permanently stuck
description:
In workflow.py (lines 351-355), if unassign_item() throws an exception during the finally block, the item remains assigned to a dead agent indefinitely. There is no retry mechanism, no persistent tracking of failed unassigns, and no periodic recovery process.

**Impact:** Over time, items accumulate in an assigned-to-dead-agent state. These items will never appear in 'bd ready' output, effectively becoming invisible to the orchestrator. This gradually reduces the pool of available work and requires manual intervention to fix (bd update <id> --unassign).

**Root cause:** The unassign failure is caught and logged as a warning (line 355) but never retried or tracked for later recovery.

**Fix options (pick one or combine):**
1. **Retry with backoff:** Retry unassign_item() 2-3 times with exponential backoff before giving up
2. **Persistent tracking:** Write failed unassign item IDs to a manifest file (similar to add_uncleaned_worktree pattern), then have the orchestrator periodically retry them
3. **Startup recovery:** On orchestrator startup, scan for items assigned to agents that no longer exist and auto-unassign them

Option 3 is recommended as it handles all causes of stuck items, not just unassign failures.

**Affected file:** src/pokepoke/workflow.py lines 351-355
close_reason: Fixed: added retry with backoff and persistent recovery for failed unassigns

title: Code Review: formatModelName drops Claude integer versions
description:
`desktop/src/utils/agentHelpers.ts` now tries to preserve version info when formatting model names, but Claude models that end with a bare integer (e.g., `claude-4`) still render as just "Claude". The fallback regex at lines ~206-210 requires the digits to be followed by a non-digit character, so identifiers that end with the version never match. As a result, the UI once again fails to distinguish Claude 3 vs Claude 4, defeating the intent of 9d557a5.

Repro:
1. Call `formatModelName("claude-4")` (or `claude-2`).
2. Expected "Claude 4" (or "Claude 2"), but the function returns "Claude".

Impact: agents running newer Claude releases are indistinguishable in the UI, so operators cannot confirm which model is actually in use, and A/B test runs become misleading.

Suggested fix: adjust the fallback regex to allow the version to terminate the string (e.g., `/claude-(\d+)(?:[^0-9]|$)/`), or extract the trailing digits with a more general pattern before returning the formatted name.

title: SDK 30-second idle completion timeout causes premature session termination
description: The SDK event handler (sdk_event_handler.py) uses a 30-second idle_timeout to detect session completion. When a session.idle event fires with pending_tool_calls==0, check_still_idle() sleeps 30 seconds then marks the session done. This is too aggressive: (1) Copilot may take >30s processing large context between tool calls (LLM thinking time). (2) While protected during active tool execution (pending_tool_calls>0), the gap between tool completion and next tool request is vulnerable. (3) In run 20260305_122045_a7e313f7, 8 of 13 items failed (62% failure rate) with 3 attempts each, many while agents were actively making progress. Sessions that appeared to be doing useful work were reported as failures, wasting significant compute. (4) The activity_watchdog uses last_event_time but should use last_tool_activity_time which is tracked but unused. Fix: (1) Increase idle_timeout to 60-90 seconds to accommodate LLM thinking time. (2) Make idle_timeout configurable via ProjectConfig. (3) Have activity_watchdog use last_tool_activity_time for more accurate detection.
close_reason: Increased idle timeout from 30s to 90s (configurable via activity_watchdog.idle_timeout_seconds), switched watchdog to use last_tool_activity_time, downgraded noisy session.idle messages to debug

This happens because the emoji is stored as surrogate pairs (\ud83d\udc4b) which cannot be encoded to UTF-8 directly. The terminal's encoding may not support surrogates. Fix options: use the actual Unicode character instead of escape sequences, or wrap the print in a try/except, or set the output encoding explicitly.

title: Worktrees created from stale ameliapayne/dev instead of master (default branch)
description: get_preferred_branch() in config.py auto-detects git username and returns '{username}/dev' as preferred branch. This causes create_worktree() to base new worktrees on ameliapayne/dev (commit 0166d8d) instead of master (6888e77). The dev branch is 20+ commits behind master, so all new work starts from stale code. Root cause: GitConfig.get_preferred_branch() line 114 returns '{username}/dev' when default_branch is not explicitly set. The auto-detect logic was intended for personal dev branches but is wrong for worktree base — worktrees should always branch from the repo's actual default branch (master). Fix: get_preferred_branch() should not be used as worktree base. create_worktree should use origin/HEAD or the configured fallback_branch (master) as base, not the user's personal dev branch.
close_reason: Invalid: ameliapayne/dev is the intended worktree base branch for this repo. The auto-detection in get_preferred_branch() is working as designed. The dev branch was temporarily stale at the time of filing but that was a transient state, not a code bug.

title: Code Review: SessionStats run counters ignore attribute assignment
description:
Regression from src/pokepoke/types.py agent-run refactor.
- SessionStats.__getattr__ proxies *_agent_runs reads to agent_run_counts, but there is no matching __setattr__.
- Callers such as tests/test_desktop_api.py::test_live_stats_update_in_realtime still mutate the live stats via stats.work_agent_runs += 1 and stats.gate_agent_runs += 2. After the refactor this only creates ad-hoc attributes on the instance; the canonical agent_run_counts dict (copied by SessionStats.snapshot() and consumed by desktop_api_stats.snapshot_to_dict) stays at zero.
- Result: DesktopAPI.get_state()[\"stats\"][\"work_agent_runs\"] never increments between polls anymore unless the caller invokes record_agent_run, breaking live stats/UI telemetry and backwards compatibility.

Repro:
from pokepoke.types import SessionStats, AgentStats
stats = SessionStats(agent_stats=AgentStats())
stats.work_agent_runs += 1
stats.snapshot().agent_run_counts[\"work\"] == 0  # should be 1, UI now stuck at 0

Fix: override SessionStats.__setattr__ (and/or add a helper) so that any *_agent_runs assignment writes through to agent_run_counts (and agent_type_elapsed_seconds, etc.), or migrate all callers before removing the legacy attrs. Until then live stats are broken.
notes: Work in progress: Investigated the issue. Confirmed SessionStats.__getattr__ proxies to agent_run_counts dict, but lacks corresponding __setattr__. Mutations via stats.work_agent_runs += 1 create ad-hoc attributes instead of updating the canonical dict. snapshot() returns zero values. Fix: implement __setattr__ to route *_agent_runs assignments to agent_run_counts dict.

title: Tests write to real .pokepoke/logs/ directory, creating 3885 directories
description: Root cause: The 35+ simultaneous log directories per timestamp are from pytest running test_orchestrator.py (29 tests), test_signal_handlers.py (1 test), and test_orchestration_flow.py (5 tests) in parallel via pytest -n auto. Each test calls run_orchestrator() which creates a real RunLogger at .pokepoke/logs/ because RunLogger is never mocked. Evidence: log content shows test fixtures (task-1, Task), test agent names (pokepoke_test_agent_1234, Janitor), 0.0 minute durations (mocked work), and the count (35) matches the exact number of run_orchestrator() calls in tests. Of 3885 total directories, the vast majority are from test runs, not production use. Fix: (1) Patch RunLogger in test conftest.py to use tmp_path instead of .pokepoke/logs/. (2) Add .pokepoke/logs/ to .gitignore if not already. (3) Consider adding a cleanup command to purge old test-generated logs. Files: tests/conftest.py, tests/test_orchestrator.py, src/pokepoke/logging_utils.py.
close_reason: Fixed: tests now use tmp_path instead of writing to real .pokepoke/logs/ directory

title: Add lock contention monitoring to coordination.py

Wrap acquire_lock to record (lock_name, wait_duration, acquired_or_timeout) and surface via stats endpoint. Track stale lock clearance frequency and histogram of lock acquisition times.

title: Maintenance agent frequencies not respected - using global modulo instead of last-run state
description:
Bug: Maintenance agents are scheduled using naive modulo arithmetic (items_completed % frequency), but this doesn't account for when agents actually last ran.

The maintenance_state.py file has infrastructure to track last_*_run counters, but this is never used. The fix should:
1. Compare current items_completed against the stored last_run value for each agent
2. Only run agent if (current - last_run) >= frequency
3. Update last_run after agent completes successfully

Current behavior: Agents may never run if the total never hits a multiple of their frequency, or may run more often than intended if the modulo happens to align.

Expected behavior: Each agent respects its configured frequency based on actual work items processed since it last ran.

Example: If Janitor (frequency=2) last ran at item 5, it should next run at item 7, then 9, etc. Not at items where 7 % 2 == 0 or 9 % 2 == 0.
close_reason: Using global modulo is acceptable for current needs - maintenance agent frequencies work fine with the modulo approach

title: Add ESLint rule to ban inline styles in desktop React components

Inline styles bypass CSS organization, make theming impossible, and produce inconsistent UI. Options: (1) Install eslint-plugin-react and enable react/forbid-dom-props with forbid: ['style']. (2) Or use a simpler custom rule/pattern. (3) Ensure existing components are clean (fix any current violations). (4) The rule should error (not warn) to enforce on commit. This pairs with the lint pre-commit check (PokePoke-ggbj) to block commits with inline styles.

title: Bug: Parallel timeout abandons running workers causing lost results and potential repo corruption
description: In parallel.py, when the 5-minute timeout fires during cleanup (line 380), remaining worker futures are silently abandoned. The code prints a warning and falls through to executor.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=False) at line 387, which does NOT stop running workers. Those orphaned threads continue executing process_work_item() (creating worktrees, running copilot, attempting merges) with no coordination or result collection.
close_reason: Fixed worker thread abandonment on timeout. Now properly cancels remaining futures and waits for them to finish before shutting down executor.

title: Migrate beads coordination print() warnings to logger
description:
beads_management.py, beads_query.py, and beads_hierarchy.py use only print() for warnings and errors. These are the most operationally critical events in the system (race conditions, claim failures, sync failures) but they are never written to disk.

Specific events to migrate to logger.warning/logger.error:
- beads_management.py: race condition detection, claim verification failure, bd sync non-zero return, failed assign/unassign/close/comment
- beads_query.py: 'beads ready command failed', timeout, parse failure, stats failure
- beads_hierarchy.py: 'Failed to check dependencies', failed to close parent

These modules currently have no 'import logging' at all - that needs to be added too.

Priority is p1 because these are the events you most need in post-hoc debugging of coordination failures.

Prerequisite: PokePoke-pvvk (handler configuration) must be done first so logger.warning calls reach the console.
close_reason: Migrated coordination warnings/errors from print() to logger

title: Worktree resource leak in agent_runner.py - missing try-finally cleanup
description:
In agent_runner.py _run_worktree_agent(), a worktree is created at line 184 but exception handling lacks a try-finally pattern to guarantee cleanup. If invoke_copilot() throws at line 196, the exception is caught and a failed CopilotResult is created, but execution continues to run_cleanup_loop() at line 208 and further logic. If any of that subsequent code raises an unhandled exception, the worktree is permanently leaked on disk.

More critically, when result.success is False (line 310-313), cleanup_worktree is called, but the success path (lines 213-308) has multiple exit points (return None at lines 244, 247, 249, 299, 306) where the worktree is intentionally preserved for 'manual intervention' but never tracked for later automated cleanup.

Fix: Wrap the entire body after worktree creation in a try-finally block. In the finally, check whether the worktree was already cleaned up (via a local flag) and force-clean if not. Track uncleaned worktrees in a manifest file for the orchestrator to clean on next startup.

Key file: src/pokepoke/agent_runner.py, lines 180-314
Severity: High - disk space leak and stale worktrees accumulate over time

title: Persist A/B model performance stats across runs in .pokepoke directory
description: Currently model A/B stats (success rate, duration, retries, etc.) are only tracked per-session in SessionStats and lost when the process exits. We need persistent storage so we can track model performance over time across many runs. Design: (1) Store stats in .pokepoke/model_stats.json (or similar) - tracks per-model: total_items_attempted, total_items_succeeded, total_items_failed, total_duration_seconds, total_retries, average_duration, success_rate, last_used timestamp. (2) On each work item completion, update the persistent stats file atomically (read-modify-write with file locking). (3) On startup, load historical stats and use them to inform model selection (e.g. weight toward models with higher success rates). (4) Include a way to view stats: bd-style command or a section in the desktop UI dashboard. (5) Stats should survive across sessions, branches, and worktrees since .pokepoke/ is in the main repo. (6) Consider a simple append-log format for raw data plus a computed summary, to avoid data loss on crashes.

title: Zero test coverage for merge conflict recovery paths in worktree_finalization.py
description:
Lines 117-177 of worktree_finalization.py contain the most complex and dangerous code in the codebase: the merge conflict detection -> cleanup agent -> abort -> retry flow. This code has 6+ conditional branches but the critical paths have **zero test coverage**.

The root cause: tests in test_workflow.py never mock `is_merge_in_progress()` or `abort_merge()`. Since tests run against a real git repo (no merge in progress), these functions return False/no-op, meaning:
- The conflict detection branch (lines 119-126) is never exercised
- The cleanup-succeeded-but-merge-still-in-progress path (lines 152-159) is never exercised
- The abort_merge() calls on lines 155, 169, 176 are never reached
- The PokePoke-o13s bug (abort_merge return value ignored) lives in these exact untested lines

**Impact:** Any fix to PokePoke-o13s or the merge conflict recovery logic has no regression safety net. Bugs in this code path mean lost work (failed merges, stuck MERGING state, orphaned worktrees).

**Required fix:**
Add tests to test_workflow.py (or a new test_worktree_finalization.py) that mock:
1. `is_merge_in_progress` returning True
2. `abort_merge` returning (True, '') and (False, 'error')
3. `invoke_merge_conflict_cleanup_agent` succeeding/failing
4. Retry merge succeeding/failing after cleanup

These tests should cover all 6+ branches in the conflict recovery flow.
close_reason: Added comprehensive test coverage for merge conflict recovery paths in worktree_finalization.py (lines 117-177). Tests cover all 6+ branches including conflict detection, cleanup agent invocation, abort_merge() return value handling, and retry scenarios.

title: Critical test coverage gap in worktree/merge data-integrity paths
description:
## Problem

The most reliability-critical code paths in PokePoke have the lowest test coverage in the project:

- **worktrees.py** (create/merge/cleanup lifecycle): **5.7%** coverage (194 statements)
- **copilot_sdk.py** (SDK communication): **10.7%** (197 stmts)
- **worktree_merge_handler.py** (core merge logic, 'single source of truth'): **11.8%** (85 stmts)
- **cleanup_agents.py** (recovery after failures): **11.6%** (155 stmts)
- **merge_conflict.py** (conflict handling): **13.6%** (59 stmts)
- **worktree_cleanup.py** (cleanup tracking): **16.2%** (160 stmts)
- **agent_runner.py** (maintenance agents): **13.5%** (200 stmts)

Overall project coverage: **52%** vs the 80% quality gate target.

## Impact

These files manage the entire worktree lifecycle: creation, agent invocation, merge to target branch, conflict resolution, and cleanup. A regression in any of these paths can cause:
- **Repository corruption** from failed merges leaving dirty state
- **Data loss** from orphaned worktrees with uncommitted work
- **Branch accumulation** from failed cleanup operations
- **Silent failures** in the merge queue that go undetected

The 80% quality gate only enforces coverage on **newly modified** files, so this legacy debt persists unchecked. Code changes to these files get the new code tested but the surrounding untested logic remains a blind spot.

## Recommendation

1. Prioritize test coverage for **worktrees.py** and **worktree_merge_handler.py** first — these manage git state mutations
2. Add integration-style tests for the merge sequence (checkout, pull --rebase, merge --no-ff, push)
3. Test error recovery paths: failed rebase abort, dirty worktree detection, uncleaned manifest tracking
4. Test the merge_queue worker loop including rebase-then-merge flow
5. Consider adding a coverage floor check for critical files (not just modified files)

title: Maintenance agents should not be scheduled after 'Stop after current item' is requested
description:
When the user selects 'Stop after current item' from the UI, the orchestrator sets should_stop_after_current() = True and intends to drain in-flight workers and exit cleanly. However, if an in-flight worker completes before the drain, record_fn fires and run_periodic_maintenance() may trigger a maintenance agent (Tech Debt, Janitor, etc.) — potentially kicking off a long-running agent that runs well past when the user expected pokepoke to stop.

Root cause: run_periodic_maintenance() is called unconditionally inside record_fn regardless of should_stop_after_current() state. The stop-after-current check in the main loop (parallel.py) only gates new work item submission, not maintenance scheduling.

Fix: In run_periodic_maintenance() (or its call site in orchestrator.py), add a guard: if should_stop_after_current(): return early without launching any maintenance agents.

This suggests an initialization or configuration error - possibly missing prompt files, misconfigured agent parameters, or a failure to launch the copilot CLI process. The janitor agent which ran just before them also failed (but after 40+ minutes of work), so there may be a shared resource exhaustion or rate limiting issue. These agents should either (1) succeed and do their maintenance work, or (2) fail with a clear error message explaining why they couldn't start.

Fix: Create an AgentContext dataclass that holds per-agent state: agent_id, work_item, log_buffer, cwd. Use threading.local() to store the active AgentContext per thread. Modify PrintRedirect.write() to read the current thread's AgentContext and route to the correct panel/buffer. Each agent thread sets its AgentContext at start via a context manager. The orchestrator thread keeps its own context. This replaces the current global ui.active_target pattern. Key files: textual_ui.py (PrintRedirect class, ~line 40), textual_app.py (message routing). The AgentContext should live in a new module or in types.py.

title: SDK event handler aggressively times out agents that are still working

It schedules completion confirmation after idle_timeout (default 10s) or turn_end_completion_timeout (0.5-5s). When an agent is thinking/planning between tool calls, these short timeouts cause premature session termination. Already observed 5+ agents killed mid-work. The _schedule_completion function checks if event_count changed and pending_tool_calls==0, but this doesn't account for the assistant composing a long response or deliberating between tool calls. Needs longer timeouts or smarter heuristics to distinguish genuine idle from inter-tool-call thinking.

title: Semaphore leak in parallel.py when executor.submit() throws between acquire and submit
description:
In parallel.py lines 193-199, semaphore.acquire() is called BEFORE xecutor.submit(). If xecutor.submit() raises an exception (e.g., executor shutting down, RuntimeError), the semaphore is never released. This causes thread starvation - the semaphore count permanently decreases by 1 per failure, eventually blocking all parallel work.

**Current code:**
\\\python
semaphore.acquire()  # Line 193 - acquired
fut = executor.submit(  # Line 194 - if this throws...
    _parallel_process_item,
    item, run_logger, semaphore, active_ids, active_ids_lock,
    worker_name,
)
# ... semaphore is released inside _parallel_process_item's finally block
# But if submit() fails, _parallel_process_item never runs = semaphore leaked
\\\

**Fix:** Wrap submit in try-except and release semaphore on failure:
\\\python
semaphore.acquire()
try:
    fut = executor.submit(
        _parallel_process_item,
        item, run_logger, semaphore, active_ids, active_ids_lock,
        worker_name,
    )
    futures[fut] = item
except Exception:
    semaphore.release()
    raise
\\\

**Impact:** In long-running autonomous sessions, accumulated semaphore leaks gradually reduce parallelism to zero, requiring a full restart.

title: Code Review: Merge lock stale timeout breaks active merges
description:
## Problem
`merge_lock()` now calls `acquire_lock(..., stale_timeout=_MERGE_LOCK_STALE_AGE)` (src/pokepoke/coordination.py lines ~70-135). `acquire_lock()` forcibly deletes the lock file whenever its mtime is older than the provided stale timeout. Because `_MERGE_LOCK_STALE_AGE` is hard-coded to 900 seconds (15 minutes), any merge or cleanup flow that legitimately holds the lock longer than that window will have its lock file unlinked by the next contender, even though the owning process is still alive.

`handle_worktree_merge()` holds `merge_lock` for the entire merge/corrective cycle, including Copilot cleanup agents and conflict resolution retries. Those agents routinely run longer than 15 minutes. With the new stale deletion enabled by default, a second agent arriving at the 15-minute mark removes the lock file and acquires `merge_lock` concurrently with the first agent, re-introducing the concurrent merge corruption this lock is supposed to prevent.

## Impact
Long-running merges or cleanup agents (>15 minutes) are now treated as “stale” and can be preempted. Once the stale threshold is crossed, two independent merges run against the same main repo, racing on `.git/index`, the worktree manifest, and the merge queue. That can corrupt the repository or leave the merge queue in an inconsistent state.

## Recommendation
Do not enable unconditional stale lock deletion for `merge_lock`. Only break the lock when you can prove the owner is gone (e.g., store the owning PID in the lock file and confirm the process has exited) or gate the behavior behind an explicit manual recovery command. At a minimum, stop passing `stale_timeout` for `merge_lock` so the existing timeouts continue to block rather than deleting the file under an active merge.

title: Copilot CLI hangs indefinitely waiting for model response - no watchdog
description: Agent icm_queue_c#-tivm froze for 22+ minutes (15:58:59 -> 16:20+) after tests passed and git status returned successfully. The Copilot CLI subprocess was alive but made an LLM API call that never returned a response. Root cause: after receiving a large tool result (14 modified files in git status), the model API call hung. PokePoke has no mechanism to detect when the Copilot CLI is running but has produced no new log output for an extended period. This is distinct from the pytest hang (which was a subprocess producing no output) - here the Copilot CLI itself is the hung process, stuck waiting on the model API. Fix: add an activity watchdog that monitors item log file mtime (or Copilot stdout) and kills/retries the Copilot session if no new output is seen for N minutes (suggested: 10-15 min threshold).
close_reason: Implemented activity watchdog to detect and abort hung Copilot CLI sessions. The watchdog monitors log file mtime and aborts sessions with no output for 10+ minutes.

title: Add per-worker activity timeout to kill workers that produce no output
description: Problem: In run 20260224_171341, worker-6 (fa9l0) was submitted at 19:42 with 0 agent requests. It never produced output but remained active in the worker pool for 14h56m, keeping the orchestrator in an idle polling loop. It was only killed when the 5-minute shutdown timeout fired at 11:00. The existing hung_command_detector (300s cumulative timeout, max_retries=3) only monitors CLI commands, not worker-level activity. Implementation: (1) Track last_activity_time per worker in the parallel executor. Update it when the worker logs output, makes an agent request, or produces a result. (2) Add a watchdog thread that checks all active workers every 60s. If a worker has had no activity for a configurable threshold (default: 10 minutes), cancel its future and log a warning. title: Non-atomic JSON manifest writes risk corruption on crash
description:
Two manifest files use direct open()+json.dump() instead of the atomic write-then-rename pattern, risking data corruption if the process crashes mid-write or if a parallel agent reads a partially-written file.

Affected files:
- worktree_cleanup.py:save_worktree_manifest() (line 134) — tracks orphaned worktrees
- beads_recovery.py:_save_failed_unassign_manifest() (line 41) — tracks stuck items needing recovery

The correct pattern already exists in this codebase at session_journal.py:105-108:
`python
tmp = path.with_suffix('.tmp')
tmp.write_text(json.dumps(...), encoding='utf-8')
tmp.replace(path)  # atomic on both Unix and Windows NTFS
``n
The manifest save functions instead do:
`python
with open(manifest_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
``n
Impact: If the process crashes during json.dump(), the manifest file is truncated/corrupt. On next startup, load_worktree_manifest() returns {} (line 131 catches JSONDecodeError), silently losing all tracked orphaned worktrees. Those worktrees then leak permanently — disk fills up, git worktree list grows unbounded, and future worktree creation may fail.

The filelock via manifest_lock() protects against concurrent writers but does NOT protect against mid-write crash corruption.

Fix: Apply the same tmp+rename pattern from session_journal.py to both save functions. Estimated effort: ~30 minutes.
close_reason: Fixed: both save_worktree_manifest() and _save_failed_unassign_manifest() now use atomic tmp+rename pattern

title: Auto-commit of main repo during active workers triggers expensive cleanup agents

When uncommitted changes are found (often from worker merges or beads sync), it tries auto-commit which runs full pre-commit hooks. Under load (8 workers active), these hooks frequently timeout or fail (resource exhaustion, mypy errors from partially-merged code), triggering a cleanup agent - a full Copilot CLI invocation that takes 4+ minutes just to commit or revert trivial changes. In run 20260225_124336_b067fa56, 2 cleanup agents were launched: one because Skipped Tests check timed out under resource pressure, another because a worker merge introduced a mypy violation. Each cleanup agent wastes time and money. Fix options: (1) Defer auto-commits until worker count drops below a threshold. (2) Use a lightweight commit path (--no-verify or reduced hooks) for auto-generated/beads-only commits. (3) Distinguish beads-only changes (.beads/ files) from source changes and skip hooks for the former. (4) Don't auto-commit while workers are actively running - wait for a quiet period.
